portraits.name: Argive Watchman
portraits.brief: A watchman keeps the beacon account and introduces the three separate household roads.

portraits.name: Cassandra
portraits.brief: Cassandra speaks within Aeschylus’s recalled homecoming, before she enters the house.

portraits.name: Clytemnestra
portraits.brief: Clytemnestra gives her own claim within the Aeschylus account.

portraits.name: Argive Housekeeper
portraits.brief: An original surviving witness keeps the household record and chooses her own shelter.

portraits.name: Pylades
portraits.brief: Pylades tells his own advice and the later source ending in Aeschylus’s tomb account.

portraits.name: Cilissa
portraits.brief: The nurse remembers the palace message and speaks for the work of care.

portraits.name: Chrysothemis
portraits.brief: Chrysothemis gives her own answer to Electra in Sophocles’s palace account.

portraits.name: The Tutor
portraits.brief: The tutor names his false death report and the urn in Sophocles’s account.

portraits.name: The Farmer
portraits.brief: The farmer offers food and dignity in Euripides’s farmhouse account.

portraits.name: The Old Servant
portraits.brief: The old servant names the scar and its childhood cause in Euripides’s account.

portraits.name: Clytemnestra
portraits.brief: Clytemnestra gives her own answer in the farmhouse telling before its later ending is heard.

portraits.name: Pylades
portraits.brief: Pylades carries the farmhouse source account, including the Dioscuri’s ending.

portraits.name: Hermione
portraits.brief: Hermione introduces Euripides’s sixth-day Orestes as a separate song. Her present consent belongs to the game’s care scenes.

portraits.name: The Phrygian Servant
portraits.brief: The servant gives his own account of the palace attack and may agree to a safe walk.

portraits.name: Pythian Priestess
portraits.brief: The priestess receives a refuge branch and introduces the Delphi opening of Eumenides.

portraits.name: The Furies
portraits.brief: The accusing chorus speaks as a group and can agree to bring its claim to Ares Hill.

portraits.name: Athena
portraits.brief: Athena names the court’s source frame, its verdict and the separate settlement.

portraits.name: Iphigenia
portraits.brief: Iphigenia tells the Tauris account in which Artemis saved her at Aulis. Every family recognition keeps this frame.

portraits.name: Thoas
portraits.brief: Thoas hears the rite at the shore and gives his own answer to a new pact.

portraits.name: The Captive Women
portraits.brief: The captive Greek women keep their own claim to return and choose whether to join a new pact.

scenery.name: Ares Hill
scenery.brief: A stone court stands above Athens. Each case names its speaker, time and claim.

scenery.name: Argive Refuge
scenery.brief: A sheltered court receives witnesses. Hermione keeps the sixth-day play within its named song.

scenery.name: Taurian Shore
scenery.brief: Salt water reaches the temple steps. Thoas hears the rite and the keepers’ reply.
